what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/check-against-a-persons-rules-and-verdicts: what each tool does, what it takes and gives back, and how it runs.

payload.label: Check words or anything made against a person's own rules and verdicts
payload.job: Check words, a title, a script line or a plan against a person's own rules and the verdicts they already gave, and say pass, fail or uncertain for each, with why
payload.description: Give the units to check (each { text, kind } or { view, kind } for JSON such as a plan, with optional facts, field, context and findings you already have), rules (rule rows judge-words runs, and ask rows a model answers), and the person's own rule document (verdict_rules) and stands (stances, as tool:read-where-you-stand gives them), read at run time from their records or files. Or give a branch in place of rules and verdict_rules: one of the person's branch rows (a node of kind branch in their one Checks list, list:checks, such as the kind of thing being made: a book, a script, an article, a post), and the rules are read from their own records: one tree in one list, every node naming the node it is part_of; the rows part_of that branch or a branch it is part_of, each branch read on its own (a branch below is never judged), plus the rows of every list a branch names in check_lists; step rows (questions of a decision step) and rows set Off are left out, a row that states no test (no words, pattern, exact, check, groups, path, evidence, ask or part) but says something is a reading row: a question a model answers once for each whole unit, made from the tool's own DATA over the row's words, carrying the calibration and model of the nearest branch's reading_settings, and listed in read_by_a_model; a piece of a source file, or a row that says nothing, is never judged: it is counted in rows_used.skipped.no_test, and a branch with only such rows answers no-applicable-rule; and the rows of the nearest branch carrying judge_settings (and of the branches extending it) are their verdict rows under those settings, the inherited rows generic rules. The answer then adds branch, lineage (nearest first) and rows_used. Their exact stand on a thing decides first: disagree fails, partly holds at review and fails at final, agree passes and clears the generic rules they named. Then their stated rows fail and their inferred rows (at_most uncertain) only hold. Nothing passes on silence: a thing nothing of theirs judges is novel, and an ask row never passes without a calibrated answer. The answer lists the questions a model may answer, by id; send the answers back in answers to use them. With branch the questions of a branch of hundreds of reading rows come in pages that each fit one answer: one entry for each rule (its ask said once, what every rule shares once in ask_all, a unit's own words never copied), and questions_page.next is the questions_after of the next call. Nothing about any person is built in.

rules.description: Rule rows: judge-words rows (see tool:judge-against-rules), each optionally with held_when ({ path, where } over a unit's facts: its findings there only hold), or ask rows { id, kinds?, says, ask: { question, options, fail, at_most?, calibration: { status, t_pass, t_fail } } }

also_found.description: Findings you already have for this unit, each with outcome fail or uncertain

A pair naming no current exact stand is refused.

payload.label: Check copy before a person reads it
payload.job: Check text, Markdown, pages, JSON, decks and picture readings against the rules you send, and the whole set against your required lines, audience, offers and counts, and say pass, fail, held or uncertain for each unit
payload.description: Give words as text, texts, Markdown, value (any JSON; fields names which keys hold words, or "strings" for every string), units, sources (JSON with its place), html (pages), decks (a rendered deck's HTML) or pictures with their readings. Markdown reads headings, paragraphs, list items, table cells and fenced display text; unresolved quotes, preamble before a declared document title and unsupported blocks stay coverage problems. It retains each block's role and field; for findings whose context is not established, name the matching rule ids or grammar check names for review, which keeps those findings uncertain and leaves other findings in force. Give rules (one row each: words, pattern, exact or a named grammar check) or leave them out to use mechanical grammar rows. Optionally give required (locked lines, features, baseline ids, approvals with the person's own words and the text they sit in), audience, offers and counts, and the person's verdict_rules and stands. Nothing about any person is kept here; their rules are input. A source with no words, a required line gone, a row for the wrong audience, a count that is not a published list view, an offer listing fewer lines than the others and a picture with no reading are problems, never passes. Model questions come back as questions; send answers on a second run.

rules.description: Rule rows, as tool:judge-against-rules takes them, with an optional not_for_kinds list. Left out: mechanical grammar rows.

kind.description: The kind of every word that names none (default copy)

fields.description: Markdown block role to source field mapping, such as heading to title and paragraph to body

context_requires_review_rules.description: Rule ids whose findings need context review on every Markdown unit in this document

markdown.description: Markdown documents: { text, where, kind, heading_kind, display_kind, document_heading_level, document_heading_is_metadata, quote_kind, fields, context_requires_review_rules }. Unresolved quotes and unsupported blocks are coverage problems; sentence-specific check findings on headings, list items, table cells and display text stay uncertain for context review.

value.description: Any JSON whose strings a person reads

fields.description: Which keys of value hold words, or "strings"

units.description: Ready-made units: { text, kind, where, facts }

alt_keys.description: Keys whose strings are picture descriptions (kind alt)

sections.description: Markdown made of declared sections: { text, where, profile: { title_kind, sections: [{ heading, kind, heading_kind?, keeps_headings? }], required?, fields? } }. Preamble and source quotes are counted and never judged; an unknown section, a missing required section, a missing title or an empty body is a problem.

cue_narration.description: Narration split into cue headings: { text, where, profile: { kind, field?, cue_heading_level, cue_id_pattern, frontmatter?: { fields: { name: string|number }, required? } } }. Each unit keeps its cue_id; quotes, code, lists, text outside a cue, empty or repeated cues and unreadable frontmatter are problems.

payload.label: Split a document into its pieces
payload.job: Split a document into its smallest self-contained pieces and keep each as the row a person keeps, so every check can name the piece it came from
payload.description: Give one of the person's files by name (as /folder/file.md, read through their files door page by page, so a file of any size up to 4 MB is never sent in one request body), or the text of a short document (Markdown), and optionally its file name and its identity. Each paragraph, list item, table row or fenced block (``` or ~~~, as CommonMark fences them) under its headings is one piece; titles, rules and table headers are not. Every piece is kept in one call as a row of the person's Checks list (record:check:piece- and the first 24 hex of its identity, kind piece): says (its lead), text, identity (1f: and the BLAKE3 of its whitespace-folded text), key (its heading path and lead), sources (the file, the piece's key there as section, the file identity and the line where it starts), and empty tags, kinds and checked_by for the person to fill. A piece already kept keeps its checked_by, no_check, tags and kinds and gains this file as a source; the same text twice is one row with two sources. Every write is conditional on what was read and fits one door message. The answer counts the pieces (new, found again as a source, unchanged), names the first ids and any piece too large for one write; tool:check-every-piece-is-covered then says what each piece lacks.

name.description: The name of one of the person's files to split, as /folder/file.md, read by reference through their files door

text.description: The words of a short document, as Markdown, in place of name (a request body over 64 KiB is refused by the door: send name for a larger file)

file.description: The document's name kept in each piece's sources; name when left out

file_identity.description: The document's identity (1f: and 64 hex); the identity of its bytes when left out

pieces.description: The pieces of the document, one per identity

sources_added.description: Rows already kept that gained this file as a source

unchanged.description: Rows already kept with this source as it is

ids.description: The first piece ids, in reading order

payload.label: Check every piece of a person's files has a check or a reason
payload.job: Say, for each of a person's source files, how many of its pieces have a check, how many a recorded reason, and which are uncovered
payload.description: Reads, through the person's records door, read only and in bounded pages, the ids of their Checks list and then its rows whose kind is piece (as tool:split-a-document-into-pieces keeps them, without their text), folding each page into a running tally, so a list of any size (40,000 rows and more) is read in one call. A piece is covered when checked_by names check rows that all exist, or when no_check has a reason (and every row its covered_by names exists). The answer: totals over every file, and per source file its pieces, those with a check, those with a reason and how many are uncovered, naming the first uncovered pieces by id, section and lead; status failed when any piece is uncovered. Checks and covered_by naming rows that do not exist are counted and the first named. The answer fits one door message (at most most_bytes of JSON): when more files remain, next is the after of the next page; with file, the page names that file's uncovered pieces by id, after after. Nothing is written.

file.description: One source file: its counts and its uncovered pieces by id, page by page

after.description: The next of the answer before: the last file shown (over every file) or the last piece named (with file)

most_bytes.description: The most bytes of JSON the answer takes (28000 when left out)

payload.label: Check a film's copy against a person's rules and verdicts
payload.job: Check every line of a film's copy files (a script table, titles, cards, a post, a description, prose or narration) against the person's own branch of their checks, with their film readers and settings
payload.description: Reads the person's settings row for this tool (list:settings, by the id given as settings_record) and the rules of one branch of their one Checks list (its own rows and every row of the branches above it; the nearest branch with judge_settings makes their verdict rows), both through their records door, read only. Reads the lines of each file handed in by the layouts their settings name (Markdown table columns by file name, fenced post text, blockquotes, paragraph files, plain lines, JSON lines), or by a declared reader (sectioned prose, cue narration, a JSON owner's paths). Marks a line the person's own recorded words when every word is in a recording span the piece's plan cites, so a row written for added words only holds there; attaches each line's context and the reader-knowledge findings it is handed. Answers per line pass, fail or uncertain with every finding, the questions a model should answer by id (send them back as answers), the report with the BLAKE3 identity of each file, the reader settings, the rules and the checker, and exit_code (0 passed, 1 failed, 2 unqualified, 3 uncertain). Nothing is written.
